title: Auto-Arena: Automating LLM Evaluations with Agent Peer Battles and Committee Discussions

bias_targets.methodology: Conducting an ablation study where two candidate models debate on separate sets of questions generated by each model, comparing their win rates to verify if models disproportionately favor or perform better on their own generated questions.
Evaluating the idiosyncratic preferences of individual LLM judges by calculating inter-judge agreement (using Cohen's Kappa) before and after introducing a multi-agent committee discussion mechanism.

Mitigating the tendency of LLM judges to prefer longer responses by imposing maximum length constraints (standardized via tiktoken) on candidate outputs and providing explicit prompt instructions to avoid length-based evaluation.
Preventing order-based preference by randomizing the presentation order of candidate models (A and B) at the start of each debate and explicitly instructing judges to avoid position biases.
